human_checks.name: A recovery-only pass on a copy of the live store: `cargo build --release -p terminus`; `copy=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/terminus-copy.XXXXXX")`; `sqlite3 "$(terminus status --json | jq -r .data.store)" "VACUUM INTO '$copy/terminus.db'"`; push one full session's watermark past its archive on the copy (the UPDATE in PLAN-2.md Notes step 4); then `TERMINUS_DATA_DIR="$copy" ./target/release/terminus ingest`, `... status`, `... status --json | jq .data.last_run.error`, `... doctor`; finally `rm -rf "$copy"`
human_checks.expected: ingest exits 0. status shows a `notes` block with a line ending `lowered`, and no `error` block unless a real transcript on the machine failed, in which case the block names only that file. `.data.last_run.error` is null when nothing failed, and doctor reports last_run ok.
human_checks.why_human: No probe exercised it. It is not irreversible, and the live store is on this machine, so it can be run instead of asked. The verifier left it out because its contract forbids mutating state and caps a check at about 10 seconds, while this check reads John's live store and writes a copy of about 3 GiB under $HOME. The commands are fully scripted in PLAN-2.md Notes, so whoever is cleared to touch the live store can run them.
